Claim 0: Hoover Dam is 660 feet thick at its base and 45 feet at its top. Supported as written.
- USGS (Lake Mead / Hoover Dam): base 660 feet thick, top 45 feet. Source: https://www.usgs.gov/media/images/lake-mead-hoover-dam
- National Park Service NRHP nomination: 660 feet thick at its base, narrowing to 45 feet at the top. Source: https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/GetAsset/NHLS/81000382_text
- ASCE landmark page gives the same. Source: https://www.asce.org/about-civil-engineering/history-and-heritage/historic-landmarks/hoover-dam

Claim 1: at 100 m deep water pressure is about 10 times the surface air pressure. Supported in a corrected form: every 10 m of water adds about one atmosphere, so at 100 m the water adds about 10 atmospheres (about 11 in total with the air).
- WHOI: pressure increases about one atmosphere for every 10 m of depth. Source: https://www.whoi.edu/know-your-ocean/did-you-know/why-is-pressure-different-in-the-ocean
- Wikipedia, Ambient pressure: about 11 atm ambient at 100 m. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambient_pressure

Claim 2: overtopping is one of the most common causes of dam failure, about a third. Supported in a corrected form: about 34 percent of dam failures (Costa 1985).
- US Bureau of Reclamation best practices D-3: Costa (1985) reported 34 percent of all dam failures were caused by overtopping. Source: https://www.usbr.gov/damsafety/Risk/BestPractices/Chapters/D3-FloodOvertoppingFailureOfDamsAndLevees.pdf
- Washington State Department of Ecology: overtopping 34 percent of all failures nationally. Source: https://ecology.wa.gov/water-shorelines/water-supply/dams/info-for-the-public/incidents-failures
